en: A golden dragon clad in the power of lightning. Highly intelligent, it rarely attacks without warning, but once battle begins it will treat you to the full course of dragon terror, breath and claws alike. Even the Kin of Darkness are wary of it.

An elf swordsman, most often in Isfald's service. Elves make up for their lack of brawn with disciplined strategy and tactics, and so crush warriors of other races who scatter and act tough. Then again, pick them off one by one and they fall easily.

A warrior swallowed up by the feel of blood and flesh in battle. It rampages with tremendous strength and physical prowess, but there is no need to meet it head-on. Put it to sleep with a spell or the like.

A swordsman baptized after swearing to fight for god. They kill and destroy for their doctrine, but with god's teachings, they never need to doubt or agonize. Only they know the worth of the 'peace of mind' they gave up their own lives to gain.
note: Kept the source's undefined [JP] as lowercase 'god' (generic deity).

en: A vicious warrior who appears with dash and flair to the brisk sound of galloping, then attacks. Like some ball game, it swings its hammer to knock adventurers' heads clean off. A small few of these warriors even dream of fighting on horseback.
note: Last sentence literal: [JP]. The 'ball game' is likely polo/croquet; kept vague as in the source.

en: An avenger: one who exacts revenge. Broadly it is not limited to warriors, but usually means those who wield the sword for vengeance. They may have their own creed, but you have no reason to die for their satisfaction. Fight fair and drive them off.

A samurai who has gained superior ability and leadership. At this rank they apparently come to hold lands of their own. They seem to enjoy having plenty of party members, and are often seen parading about in large groups.
The doors of Rubenburg are open to all. Graduating, however, is no easy matter. Can you hold on to what you feel now, full of dreams and hope, until the very end?

Students gather from all over, so their everyday clothes vary too. The school issues uniforms, but on days off everyone returns to their homeland's customs, and the school buildings apparently turn into a kind of international fashion show.
One who has trained as a Summoner and grown strong enough to bury an average adventurer single-handed. It summons one creature after another, as if building a wall of monsters.

A priestess directly under Sarijana, goddess of growth and carnal love. Her body, which enthralls man and woman alike, is a divine gift. But every rose has thorns. Master of Tarot, nuclear magic and barriers, she'll send you to heaven, body and soul.
note: [JP] = Barrier (Elm3/eboot); [JP] = nuclear magic (slice 056 'Nuclear strike spell'). [JP] double meaning kept with 'send you to heaven'.

en: A battle maiden blessed by the gods and versed in the spear. With keen insight she reads her foes' moves and cuts them down with blinding speed. Her spear reaches even the back row. Be careful if you ever have to fight one.
note: [JP] rendered 'the gods' to match the filled Valkyrie entries (MON_TEXT 'battle maiden blessed by the gods').

en: A priest who travels spreading god's teachings. So strong is their faith that at some point they learned to fly. When they find prey, they creep up without a sound, surround it with their comrades, and start talking about love.

An eastern Kannagi or Summoner, retained by royal houses and shoguns for prophecy, sorcery and divination. They usually perform all manner of rites, but when they sense a spirit, they command monsters called "Shiki" to drive the evil away.
note: [JP] = Kannagi (eboot class name). [JP] rendered 'a spirit'. [JP] -> "Shiki" ([JP] -> double quotes, [JP] -> single quotes, per translation_brief).

en: A battle maiden who mastered her path, she skewers foes on a holy spear as the gods teach. Stricter than Valkyries, she hates impurity of body and above all of soul: heart and faith. Such zeal may look comical, but have you found anything worth that faith?

A villain who prowls the labyrinth, using the dirty trick of ganging up on weakened adventurers. Individually, though, they are not very strong, so if you make full use of magic and the like, you should be able to fight them fairly safely.

A female ninja drilled in shinobi skills and mindset. She uses her womanhood as a weapon, so underestimate her and you'll pay. Stand beside her and you'll notice a faint, sweet scent at her collar. One of the few vanities a kunoichi is allowed?

A bold way of life, and the strong luck to back it up. A thief with both is called a Lucky Star. They are skilled enough to found a band of thieves of their own, and their varied fighting styles are sure to throw adventurers into a panic.

A ninja with even more training. Attack, agility, decapitation rate and many other abilities have all risen. If you meet one, do not leave it be: take it down. By the time your head has left your body, it is too late.

A demi-human monster that evolved in an unusual way. With partisan in hand it spears fish, and adventurers. It hates dryness and prefers to live in wetlands. Orcs recently taught them about seasonings, and salt-grilled fish is now all the rage.

A swift half-horse beastkin archer that hunts in packs. Its hunts usually succeed, but it is also known for lechery, carrying off adventurers stunned by poison arrows on its back to wed them. Not just women: handsome men get taken too. Such barbarians.
note: Compressed to fit: 'carry home and take as wives' folded into 'hauls off ... to make them its brides'; [JP] = stunned (paralysed) by poison arrows.

en: By kobold custom the strongest becomes King, decided by nothing less than a clan-wide brawl. Young and old, men and women all pile in, so a female King sometimes emerges. Hence most past Kings are hotheads. Only Kings may wear a red cape.
note: [JP]: 'a female King' (title kept as King, not queen).

en: The gourmet king who reigns over orc society. Perhaps eating well really does make you stronger, for the Orc King has abilities worthy of the title. Take it lightly and you will end up as their dinner.

The leader of the lizardmen. It is bigger built and more athletic than an ordinary lizardman, and no easy opponent. As befits a king, its hunting skill is beyond doubt: it can spear three fish with a single thrust.
A strange giant with two heads growing from its neck. Violent by nature, it constantly scans its surroundings with both heads. The two heads often quarrel over which one controls the body.

A one-eyed giant gifted at smithing, of an odd race whose every member can do smithing and alchemy. Gruff like most craftsmen, but mild-natured. They like to live near volcanoes, where fire is always at hand. Visit one and it may sell you a special weapon.
note: [JP] = 'smithing and alchemy' (HELP_TEXT wording).

en: An ice giant. It favors the 'Freezing Sword', which freezes what it touches, and likes to freeze foes and then shatter them. It sometimes brings seafood to the Fire Giants, who grill it piping hot at once. Inwardly it sighs: 'Raw tastes better...'
note: [JP] = Freezing Sword (ITEM). [JP] = Fire Giant (name not yet filled in MONRAW).

en: A giant shrouded in mystery. Mages and alchemists say it is a constructed giant; Summoners say it is a monster called from another world. Either way, it is surely one of the more troublesome foes adventurers face. Care to solve its mystery yourselves?

The god of life-creation, who presides over the birth of life. Ildraha has a fiery, rash side. New life is ever trying to well up from within Ildraha's body, held back only by a seal Ildraha has placed on it.
note: New name [JP] = Ildraha. No gender in source: name repeated instead of a pronoun.

en: The god of pleasure and change, who presides over the growth of life. Ashtel is Naru's older sister; the two are sister gods. A hedonist who loves uproar and chaos, she acts on likes and dislikes like a child and makes Naru clean up her messes.
note: Ashtel spelling from script slice 031. Female: [JP] / [JP].

en: The god of death, who presides over the end of life. A quiet god who watches the life and death of the world with a detached gaze, and whose body goes on receiving the 'death' of every living thing.

The god of space, who makes from nothing the space to build worlds in, and chief of the six gods. Clever but extremely pedantic, Void cannot stand anything not going exactly to design, and so resents Ildraha, who acts purely on emotion.
note: [JP] = chief god (script slice 030).

en: The god of time, who brings the flow of time to the world. Ashtel's younger sister. Naru holds an 'hourglass' called 'Tonak-Kanakol'. Void and the others must find the 'Eld' before it runs out; if they fail, the realm of the gods is said to collapse.
note: New term [JP] = Tonak-Kanakol ([JP] -> hyphen as in Espel-Dex). [JP] kept as single quotes; 'Eld' without 'the' inside the quotes.

en: The god of existence, who affirms that each thing 'is' there. Without Dehain's approval, no created thing can ever exist in the world. Whether something once approved can be 'revoked', Dehain has never tried, and so does not know.

The former god of life-creation, loving all life alike. Running for chief god to make a life paradise and the Eld, Orses won no support, clashing with Dehain. Torn by duty and heart, Orses chose heart, left hopes to an heir, and went to the event horizon.
note: Compressed. [JP] = 'running for chief god'; [JP] = 'left hopes to an heir'. [JP] = event horizon (glossary).

en: The former god of change, a goddess who dozes often and acts on dreams. One day she dreamed the gods' world fell, and grieved for life left wailing in the chaos. Keener to rebuild order after the fall than on the stalled Eld, she made a certain factor.
note: Female: [JP]. [JP] = 'life left wailing' (compressed). [JP] = 'the stalled Eld' creation.

en: The former god of space, managing space as Void does now. A god of laughter too, Semnadoc did all sorts to cheer Dehain, tormented by regret over the Urna affair. For a certain reason, Semnadoc abdicated by choice: rare, barring dismissal or no-confidence.
note: [JP] read as Dehain's own deeds (Dehain refused to approve Urna's land per glossary). [JP] -> 'rare, barring dismissal or no-confidence'.

en: The former god of time. The gods in the Creation Womb Palace are the six creation gods of Urna's birth. Of the living gods, Sinhanicol was among the closest to the birth of "Tonak-Kanakol", and is a mystery. Sinhanicol then awaited a calm, impartial heir.
note: [JP] = Creation Womb Palace (script slice 067). [JP] -> double quotes (row 283 has [JP] -> single). Last sentence compressed: [JP] -> 'a calm, impartial heir'.

en: An elder heading the Bistel royal Magic Bureau, who with its staff keeps a spell barrier on the city walls. Archelon's granddaughter fell for an adventurer and rarely visits, hence the foul mood. Is that why Archelon is hard on adventurers in the cave?
note: [JP] kept neutral (glossary: no explicit gender); name repeated instead of a pronoun. [JP] = spell barrier; [JP] = the Bureau's staff.

en: Noble dragonkind is a race apart. Proud of their neutrality, dragons shun humans and elves and should never side with the Kin of Darkness. But his forebears grew close to them, so like the Dragonfolk he is disowned by dragonkind and must live in darkness.
note: Source uses [JP] for Donnelkral (male). [JP] = Dragonfolk (script slice 039).

en: A monstrous woman serving Demon Duke Animacie. Her swift attacks from her bizarre body are unpredictable. By Espel-Dex's contract she was told to aid Zeshrom, and so joined this fight. Her aim: a cure for her master's ailing body.
note: [JP] 'monstrous woman' (glossary describes Escapra as [JP]).

en: A spectral warrior. A member of Espel-Dex, Nonhared has destroyed land after land. Zeshrom is Nonhared's direct superior, but Nonhared is not happy with the way he works.
note: [JP] = Zeshrom. Nonhared's gender not stated: name repeated.

en: A hedonist living only for fun, with no wish to serve a master. None at all. Liking this land, the Mistress kept a divine relic quiet and settled in the pleasure district. Taught a Demon Duke's daughter bad ways; now out of touch, frets like a bad pal.
note: Gender of Mistress not stated: no pronoun. [JP] -> 'kept it quiet'; [JP] -> 'frets like a bad pal'; [JP] ('this time too') dropped for space.

en: A devil of Espel-Dex. Having found a special Zefkaka, he plots to seize its power and expand Espel-Dex. A master schemer but a bit soft-hearted, he has little taste for pure destruction. His ideal is smart yet aggressive rule, and he strives for it daily.

An ancient evil spirit trying to take this land. Fiona's name was carved on the Holy Foundation, Contrachio, symbol of sovereignty over the land, but she has rewritten it with her own name to make this land hers.

The land of Zeshrom's birth was on the brink of being scrapped. To escape that, its Zefkaka set out to reset itself, cast out the life rooted in it, Zeshrom included, and rose again as a New Land. Cast off by his own land, how does Zeshrom see Urna?
note: New term [JP] = 'scrapped' (land decommissioned by the gods); not found elsewhere.

en: A Zefkaka is a land's soul or will. All Zefkaka are said to have split off from the first fragment, the Primordial Soil, and grown into lands. By an old twist of fate, this land held both Fiona's and Urna's Zefkaka. Now, which Zefkaka will you choose?
note: New term [JP] = Primordial Soil.

en: Urna, lawful sovereign of the land via the divine relics. Its life should have hailed her return, but the wall of time made it unwelcome. Fiona, who once took the New Land's rights from her, blocks her again, and in sorrow Urna swings the Sword of Wrath.
note: [JP] = Sword of Wrath (glossary item, kept by Urna).

en: One of the Four Sages of the Hestrio Continent: a giant owl who rules the wind. Possessed of much ancient wisdom, it is said to be the closest of the Four Sages to humans.

One of the Four Sages of the Hestrio Continent: a giant dog who rules fire. Fierce by nature, he lives in the Scorching Castle with the creatures who adore him. He rules fire but is no fire spirit, so when it gets too hot, he snaps.
note: Source uses [JP] for Radrecht twice (gender evidence; glossary has unknown).

en: One of the Four Sages of the Hestrio Continent: a giant jellyfish who rules water. Her coral crown lets her know the state of the whole sea. She loves quiet, and cannot stand the overbearing or the noisy.

One of the Four Sages of the Hestrio Continent: a giant mole who rules the earth. Raizam lived in the Blanc Desert but somehow never felt at home there, and wants to move away. Not very bright, but the most sensible of the Four Sages.

Leaving the Princess's land, a strange light felled us into ages of sleep. Awake, we forgot the past and guarded folk here, till a dear voice called from below!? We answer her now! I am Omsis of Wind!! "Come, Princess! Let's finish our broken dream!"
note: Shared chant rows 308-311 (and 312-315): same English opening; compressed to fit 256. New term [JP] (row name [JP]) not needed in text. [JP] dropped as 'I am'.

en: Leaving the Princess's land, a strange light felled us into ages of sleep. Awake, we forgot the past and guarded folk here, till a dear voice called from below!? We answer her now! I am Rades of Fire!! "We kept 'em safe! You'll praise us, right, Princess?"
note: Rades = Radrecht's earlier name (glossary). [JP] -> 'We kept 'em safe'.

en: Leaving the Princess's land, a strange light felled us into ages of sleep. Awake, we forgot the past and guarded folk here, till a dear voice called from below!? We answer her now! I am Shirins of Water!! "Oh Princess, this time I'll stay to the end!!"
note: Shirins = Shirinmorin's earlier name (glossary).

en: Leaving the Princess's land, a strange light felled us into ages of sleep. Awake, we forgot the past and guarded folk here, till a dear voice called from below!? We answer her now! I am Raizas of Earth!! "Welcome home, Princess~! Squeeze me, mogu~!!"
note: Raizas = Raizam's earlier name (glossary); [JP] -> 'mogu' (glossary).

en: Long ago, in a certain land, a "theorem" that could deeply affect the world of the gods was discovered. But its discoverer never realized its value, and someone stole the theorem, hid it, and sealed it away in another land.

A giant vampire bat, with more than double the strength and stamina of a normal one. But it is a coward at heart. Hiding in the depths of the cave, it lays trap upon trap on the way to its lair, then sinks its fangs into worn-out foes.

Armitt's dear, dear only son, who startles people by sticking out his tongue with a big 'blehhh'. The more trouble a child, the dearer, they say, and Armitt is always fussing over him. He has worries of his own, it seems, but none of it shows on his face.
A strange demon said to have come from a different land. It is said to twist space when it appears. It is called a demon, but rumor has it that it may be more powerful than any demon.
A demon that brings death with a grating laugh. It was granted part of the authority of the King of the Dead, and loves to wield that power to make fools of its foes.
note: [JP] = King of the Dead (= the Wraith, per row 324).

en: An old lord who joined forces with the Wraith, King of the Dead, to rescue his beloved Eril, taken by Apasha, the Abyss. He found her again, but Apasha's hold was so overwhelming that, far from saving her, he was swallowed into the Abyss with her.
note: [JP] = 'his beloved' (glossary: Eril is Branet's wife).

en: That old lord is now nothing but a pitiful soul swallowed by the Abyss. If there is any comfort left, perhaps it is that he can wander with his beloved Eril.

Hers was no special life. She simply lived as best she could, and died. But the flawed path of souls spilled her soul into the Abyss. When Branet called, she knew it was dangerous and she must not seek help, yet could not hold back her overflowing heart.
note: [JP] read as [JP] (likely typo): 'lived as best she could'.

en: The only gate linking the inside of Apasha, the Abyss, with the world of the living. Which land it appears in, when, and how long it stays open are all impossible to predict. Opening it also seems to require the dead and the living to work together.

A snow woman with an especially warm heart who falls in love easily. She saves lost travelers and gives them a night's shelter, but each parting hurts, and at night she weeps alone into her pillow, sighing as she counts the snow, hoping they'll return.
note: Compressed slightly: [JP] ('even among snow women') folded into 'especially'; the travellers' 'some day return' kept as 'hoping they will come back'.

en: Miyuki's father and head of the winter kin. He had a beautiful snow woman for a wife, but she fell ill and passed away. So dearly does he cherish Miyuki, the child she left behind, that he often acts selfishly.
note: [JP] = winter kin (script slice 047).

en: Captain Wanelly, King of Adventure. A good captain who cares for the crew, but hot-tempered and quick with fists. At last, pirates who resented him ambushed him in the Narmant Trench. He fought well but was outnumbered, and sank with ship and crew.
note: Source uses [JP] for Wanelly (gender evidence; glossary has unknown). [JP] = King of Adventure.

en: A giant bird kept beneath Baroque Fort. Goblins sometimes take it out for walks and they get along well enough, but when its stress boils over, it goes on a rampage.

A mage serving as Rubenburg's Vice Principal, second only to the Board Chair: the real No. 2. Free to set the budget, she built a big magic research wing and teaches Magic students practical skills. Her poise draws many girls to the Magic course.
note: [JP] -> 'No. 2'. [JP] = 'Magic' department (compressed). Female per glossary.

en: A teacher of the occult, Tarot above all. Scheherazade loves studying odd devices and often causes trouble; lately, made grenades with Prof. Harmoni and was punished by Kathleen. Very popular with the boys, many of whom want extra lessons.
note: No gender stated: no pronoun. [JP] read as [JP] (remedial lessons).

en: The magic school's only brawn teacher, there to teach tactics against warriors. A stiff, earnest type, McMahon frets over having to spread word of the job's weak points. It's meant to be secret, but everyone can tell, and Kathleen often offers comfort.
note: No gender stated: name, no pronoun. [JP] = McMahon's own calling (warrior).

en: An Onmyoji Special Advisor from a far eastern land. Kamikaze teaches summoning, and about the Kin of Darkness: how they appear, lead hearts astray, prey on people, and discard them when done. Kamikaze teaches much from personal experience.
note: [JP] -> Onmyoji (monster name [JP]). No gender stated.

en: The man serving as Rubenburg's Principal. He graduated top of his class and once taught. But true to the rule that "a boss with able staff goes soft", he leaves it all to Kathleen and just stamps papers, invites outside teachers on a whim, or snort-laughs.
note: [JP] -> 'snort-laughs' (script renders his [JP] as 'snort'). [JP] = man.

en: Founder of Rubenburg and ex-court mage of Isfald, versed in magic and all other knowledge. That knowledge showed that the lands do not exist for mortals; wishing to be free of the gods, the Board Chair tried to dabble in forbidden arcane experiments.
note: [JP] read as 'for mortals' (us people). [JP] ('tried to dabble') rendered 'turned to'; see report.

en: Tentacles that serve as the limbs of the Kin of Darkness, and only the mightiest of them at that. It is said that ordinary adventurers are overcome by their miasma just from laying eyes on them.

The new king of Baroque Fort. Orphaned by an epidemic, he was raised by Ubogenya. A fussy eater, he hated every meal from childhood. One day he snapped and holed up in the storehouse, but none of the food inside suited him, and the siege lasted a day.

The Ogre Lord two reigns back, who started the "A King Must Bungee" tradition. Fond of whim decrees, this Lord issued the "Goblin Warrior Act" ("Goblins must train too!"), outraging goblins and the ogres who relied on goblin support.
note: No gender in source: 'this Lord' instead of a pronoun. [JP] = two reigns back. [JP] = 'Goblin Warrior Act' (new term). [JP] = 'tradition' (literally an entertainment/custom).

en: The old goblin who raised the Goblin Prince. Strict in discipline, she was feared not only by goblins but by ogres as well. It is said there is no one whose backside Ubogenya has not smacked.
note: Ubogenya female per glossary.

en: A Kobold King, Bohinyob's friend. At bouts, crowds roared: Bohinyob's one blow, or Babis's Swallow Cut? As a child, Babis saw a samurai say "Fear not, 'twas the flat of the blade" and took up flat strikes. But the samurai was wrong, and the error lives on.
note: This entry describes Babis (glossary: kobold samurai). [JP] = Swallow Cut; [JP] = flat-of-the-blade strike (strictly the back of the blade).
